Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Four plugins of kagex's own, shipped with every engine**: [sdlsystem](https://github.com/krkren/sdlsystem), [voicefx](https://github.com/krkren/voicefx), [glitchtrans](https://github.com/krkren/glitchtrans) and [speech](https://github.com/krkren/speech), each in a repository of its own under the 0BSD licence. On Windows, Linux and Steam they're files of their own in `plugin/`, in the macOS app beside the executable; on the web, Android and iOS they're linked into the engine, as every plugin is there. A game on an older engine gets none of what they do, and nothing fails
- **Glitch transitions** (`method=glitch`): the old picture breaks up as a damaged video stream or a bad signal would, in stages, while the new one arrives in patches: a datamosh, a broken JPEG stream, damaged cells, pixel sorting, a rolling and slanting analog picture with a tracking band, bands, split colours, static and frames of signal failure. `style=` picks which lead (`mixed`, `digital`, `analog`, `mosh`), each fault has its own amount, and a seed gives the same glitch every time. A World image's or character's `trans=glitch` breaks up the whole screen. Config's Screens Change With turns the system screens' crossfades into glitches; the transitions demo shows each style
- **Voice effects**: an echo for memories, a phone's thin voice, a muffled one through a door, a hall, a cave, a radio, for one character (`[pip voicefx=phone]`) or every voice (`[env voicefx=memory]`), kept in saves and going back; subtle, so a line stays easy to follow
- **Lines read aloud with the system's voices**, for players who can't or don't want to read: each message is spoken as it waits for a click and plays like a voice line, for every line or only the unvoiced ones, with a voice, speed and pitch per character and a pronunciation list. Windows, macOS, Linux (espeak-ng), Android, iOS and the browser
- **The game in the background**: Config's In the Background keeps playing, mutes or pauses the game while its window is behind another or minimized, or a phone or a browser tab has put it away; a phone putting the game away, warning that memory is low or ending it writes the continue save at once
- **Opening pages, folders and programs**: `System.shellExecute` works on every platform; About has a Website button, the manual's links open the browser, Config opens the screenshot folder, and the Debug menu opens the script at the line the game is on
- **Screenshots** to the save folder or a folder named after the game in the player's pictures folder, and on the clipboard too; a frame-rate limit (30 or 60) for a laptop's battery
- For game makers: kagex-release makes a movie's smaller version (`<name>_sd.webm`, 540 lines) for the web, phones and players who pick it, and converts MP4, MOV, AVI and other movies to WebM, through ffmpeg; `doc/porting.txt` and `Porting.tjs` for games brought from other Kirikiri engines; web games whose file names have `%`, `#` or `?` load them
- kagex-release 0.28.0 downloads the 0.28.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.28.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
